prior_importants.description: The replay re-prices carried context as a fresh cache write when an actual automatic compaction is not taken under the replayed threshold. It should be a 0.1x cache read. This inflates the replayed spend at every threshold that skips a compaction.

If no transcript in a class started inside the window and none had an auto compaction, the reset floor is `{read: 0, write: 0}`. Every replayed reset then costs nothing, which makes the lower thresholds look like large savings.

findings.description: When the replay skips an automatic compaction, the new rule reads all of `carried` from the cache. That includes the tokens added after the previous request (`compactedContext - before`), which the replay never cached, so the step is under-priced at 0.1x instead of the write tier. The ADR line "that context is still in the cache" has the same gap. Capping the read at `Math.min(replayed, carried)` for `autoReset` steps would fix it.

`rebuilt()` now has one caller (the `kept` line). The carried-read line spells out `step.idle || step.manualReset`, which is `rebuilt()` minus `autoReset`. The same predicate is written two ways within 40 lines and the difference is not explained. Inline `rebuilt()` at its last caller, or name the narrower predicate.

The file header still says the replay re-prices "the rewrite after an idle hour". This delta extends the rewrite to a `/compact` (see the ADR and the `replayTranscript` JSDoc), so the header now understates it.
This edit leaves one line well past the ADR's ~100-column hard wrap, and the next sentence ("A request that rebuilt the cache…") is joined onto it. Re-wrap the paragraph.
